options: Prophethood and the messengers sent by God
questions.explain: Risalah is the belief in prophethood, that God sent prophets and messengers to guide humanity.

questions.q: Which three deities make up the Hindu Trimurti?
questions.explain: The Trimurti is Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver and Shiva the destroyer.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the Three Marks of Existence?
questions.explain: Anicca, meaning impermanence, is one of the Three Marks of Existence alongside anatta and dukkha.
Rosh Hashanah marks the Jewish New Year and the start of the High Holy Days.

questions.q: What does 'dharma' refer to in Hinduism?
questions.explain: Dharma refers to duty, righteousness and the proper way of living.

questions.q: How many mitzvot (commandments) does the Torah traditionally contain?
questions.explain: The Torah traditionally contains 613 mitzvot that guide Jewish life.

questions.q: In Hinduism, what is the name for the ultimate, supreme reality or spirit?
questions.explain: Brahman is the ultimate reality or supreme spirit underlying all existence in Hinduism.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the Three Refuges (Three Jewels)?
questions.explain: The Three Refuges are the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Sangha (the community of Buddhists).

questions.q: For Muslims, the Qur'an is believed to be:
options: The direct word of God revealed to Muhammad
A book written after his death by historians
questions.explain: Muslims believe the Qur'an is the literal word of God revealed to the Prophet Muhammad.

questions.q: During Sukkot, what do many Jewish families build and eat in?
questions.explain: During Sukkot families build a sukkah, a temporary hut recalling the Israelites' time in the wilderness.

questions.q: Tawhid, the most important belief in Islam, means:
questions.explain: Tawhid is the belief in the absolute oneness and unity of God (Allah).

options: The cycle of birth, death and rebirth
questions.explain: Samsara is the continuous cycle of birth, death and rebirth driven by karma.
